memory_update.text: KRT is the highest-fit underfollowed public candidate for restaurant off-premise packaging because it is small-cap, foodservice-disposables focused, and explicitly serves restaurant chains and distributors.

GPK should remain in the universe as a mid-cap paperboard foodservice/QSR packaging supplier, but its restaurant exposure requires segment-level verification because broader paperboard and consumer-packaging exposure dilutes purity.
AMCR is a large-cap reference name after the Berry Global combination; include for scaled cup/lid and QSR packaging context, but not as the primary underfollowed alpha candidate.

Foodservice distributors such as Sysco may be important route-to-market chokepoints for packaging suppliers even if they are not packaging manufacturers; later layers should map which suppliers sell through broadliners and franchise supply cooperatives.

Pactiv Evergreen/Novolex and Dart/Genpak are highly relevant private or no-longer-public foodservice packaging leaders; their presence should be used as competitive context but excluded from the US-listed candidate list unless public parent exposure can be mapped.

Next search pass should look for niche public suppliers adjacent to packaging: compostable-material inputs, molded fiber equipment, resin/recycled-polypropylene suppliers, coatings/barrier materials, and packaging distributors with restaurant customer concentration.

node: Off-premise packaging, disposables, and delivery-enabling consumables
summary: Expanded the public-company universe for restaurant off-premise packaging. The strongest underfollowed pure-play candidate found is Karat Packaging, a small-cap manufacturer/distributor of disposable foodservice products used by restaurant chains and distributors. Graphic Packaging is a mid-cap paperboard and foodservice packaging supplier with QSR exposure but broader end-market dilution. Amcor is a large-cap reference name after absorbing Berry Global, giving it direct exposure to foodservice cups/lids and QSR packaging, though the restaurant node is not pure. Sysco is included only as a reference/context anchor because its distribution network can influence restaurant procurement of food and non-food supplies, but it is not a packaging manufacturer.
